title: IC Preview — 555 Timer and 74HC595 Shift Register

zones.label: 555 Timer
zones.summary: An 8-pin DIP chip that makes timing pulses — the part behind blinkers, delays and simple tones.
facts: In astable mode it runs free, switching its output on and off over and over to make a steady stream of pulses.
In monostable mode it fires once when triggered, holding its output on for a set time and then dropping back.
Full wiring and timing math in Chapter 14.

zones.label: 74HC595 Shift Register
zones.summary: A 16-pin DIP chip that turns a handful of control wires into eight separate outputs.
facts: Serial data in: you clock bits into it one at a time, over a single data wire.
Parallel data out: once the bits are loaded it drives all eight output pins at once.
Full wiring and the 8-LED project in Chapter 15.

quiz.question: Which chip has 16 pins, with 8 down each side?
quiz.explanation: The 74HC595 is a 16-pin DIP; the 555 has only 8 pins.

quiz.question: Which chip would you reach for to make an LED blink on its own, over and over?
quiz.explanation: That is the 555 running in astable mode, producing a repeating stream of pulses.

quiz.question: Which chip lets you drive eight outputs while using only a few control wires?
quiz.explanation: A shift register takes serial data in and drives eight parallel outputs.

quiz.question: Which chip fires once when triggered and then returns to its resting state?
quiz.explanation: That is monostable mode on the 555 timer.
